title: Simplicial presheaf presentation of one-sided fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences, internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], one-sided fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the explicit coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. A Dwyer--Kan equivalence is a simplicial functor inducing weak homotopy equivalences on mapping simplicial sets and an equivalence on the categories having the same objects and path components of mapping sets as arrows. For a simplicial set $K$, its opposite has $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_n=K_n$ with faces $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and degeneracies $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$; the opposite simplicial category has $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}(x,y)=\mathcal C(y,x)$ with reversed composition. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small simplicial set $S$. The enriched category $\mathsf D_S$ consists of simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$. It has a simplicial projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations; cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial Kan fibrations. Cofibrant, fibrant and model category have the meanings of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. A simplicial model structure is enriched, tensored and cotensored over Kan-model simplicial sets with the induced mapping-space map for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either input arrow is a weak equivalence. Its mapping complex has $n$-simplices the enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. Let $\mathsf D_S^{cf}$ be its full simplicial subcategory of cofibrant-fibrant objects. Let $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ be the simplicial category of right fibrations over $S$, with mapping complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ consisting in degree $n$ of maps $X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ over $S$.

The cone functor $T:(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}\to\mathsf D_S$, $p\mapsto T_p$, has an ordinary right adjoint $U_S$. There is a simplicial structure on this unstraightening functor $U_S$ whose restriction $\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Its underlying simplicial set is specified as follows. For $p:X\to S$, put $M_p=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[S]$, write $v$ for the new cone vertex, and put $T_p(s)=M_p(s,v)$, contravariantly in $s$ by precomposition. The simplices of $U_SF$ over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are the enriched natural maps $T_\sigma\to F$; operators are induced by simplex operators. The join here has $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}X_a\times Y_b$, with ordered concatenation operators, and the pushout is the categorical colimit of simplicial categories.

For every objectwise Kan $F$, $(U_SF)_s$ is naturally weakly equivalent to $F(s)$. The functor $U_S$ carries objectwise weak equivalences between such diagrams to equivalences of right fibrations. For every map $u:B\to S$, there is a natural isomorphism $u^*U_SF\cong U_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$, compatible with composition of base maps. For a constant diagram with Kan value $X$, there is a natural map $S\times X\to U_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ which is a weak homotopy equivalence on every vertex fiber. The constructions stay in $\mathcal V$.

For any $Z\to S$ and right fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan. A map between right fibrations over $S$ is an equivalence in $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ if and only if its maps on vertex fibers are weak homotopy equivalences. Here equivalence means a simplicial map with an inverse up to simplicial homotopies over $S$. The category $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ has a simplicial contravariant model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms, weak equivalences are the maps $X\to Y$ for which $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every right fibration $Z\to S$, and fibrations are characterized by lifting against the trivial cofibrations. Its fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations, and every object is cofibrant. The adjunction $T\dashv U_S$ is a Quillen equivalence. Here Quillen equivalence means that the left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations and, for cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $F$, $TX\to F$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to U_SF$ is a weak equivalence. Tensor and enriched mapping objects in the slice are $X\times K\to S$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$.

The covariant model structure on $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ is obtained from the contravariant one over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the ordinary equivalence $X\mapsto X^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is also simplicial for the same tensor and mapping objects, all objects are cofibrant, and its fibrant objects are exactly the left fibrations. Weak equivalences between left fibrations are exactly the maps which are weak homotopy equivalences on vertex fibers. Put $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathfrak C[S],\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})$ with its simplicial projective model structure. Reversal of ordered vertex labels gives $\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S F=(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)^{\mathrm{op}}$: here $F:\mathfrak C[S]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$ is regarded, after taking opposites, as a contravariant diagram on $S^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the opposite of the resulting right fibration is a left fibration over $S$. As an ordinary functor $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ is the right adjoint in a Quillen equivalence from the covariant model structure to $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$. Its infinity functor is its right-derived functor, obtained by localizing its restriction to objectwise Kan diagrams. Its fiber at $s$ is $(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)_s^{\mathrm{op}}$, naturally equivalent as a space to $F(s)$. It preserves objectwise weak equivalences between these diagrams, and its base-change isomorphisms and size assertions are obtained by applying opposites to those for $U$. The opposite of the constant-product map is $S\times X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ and is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers. For any $Z\to S$ and left fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan; a map between left fibrations is a simplicial homotopy equivalence over $S$ if and only if it is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 (cone construction); Proposition 2.2.1.1 (base change); Proposition 2.2.3.11 (printed p.83, enriched presentation); Lemmas 2.2.3.4 and 2.2.3.6 (Kan mapping complexes and fiberwise equivalences); Remark 2.2.2.11 and Proposition 2.2.2.9 (vertex fibers and constant-product map). Projective model structure: Proposition A.3.3.2. Covariant assertions are the opposite-simplicial-set dual. Read online; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag. Model structures and Quillen equivalence: Propositions 2.1.4.7–8, Remark 2.1.4.12, Theorem 2.2.1.2, Corollaries 2.2.3.12–13; covariant adjunction is the ordinary opposite-base dual, without an assertion that the opposite operation preserves simplicial enrichment.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] only for the fact that the Kan model is combinatorial and simplicial; its ordinary-indexing presheaf theorem is not being applied to $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] to diagrams on the small simplicial category $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. This gives the asserted projective model and mapping complexes, without assuming the indexing category locally Kan. The functor $L_S$ of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] is exactly $T$ in the statement: both evaluate the same pushed-out coherent cone at $(s,v)$. Its right adjoint has exactly the simplex-family formula stated here. That node gives the ordinary adjunction and preservation of all monomorphisms as projective cofibrations. In particular $TX$ is cofibrant for every slice object $X$. Use the whole statement of the now independently split [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]: it gives the cone-defined model structure, monomorphic cofibrations, right-anodyne trivial cofibrations, fibrant objects exactly the right fibrations, their Kan vertex fibers, and detection of weak equivalences between them on vertex fibers. Every slice object is cofibrant since its initial map is monomorphic.

source.place: Sections 2.1.4 and 2.2.1; Proposition A.3.3.2; use the independent proof of Corollaries 2.2.3.12-13 already recorded in the slice node.

proof.text: The cone in [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] is $S\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)$. The colimit construction of coherent realization identifies its realization with $M_p$. By [lem-coef-cone-boundary-projective-cells], the base mapping sets are those of $\mathfrak C[S]$, there are no maps from $v$ to a base object, the endomorphisms of $v$ form a point, and the remaining mapping sets are $T_p(s)$. An induced map of these cones fixes objects and base mapping sets. It is therefore a Dwyer--Kan equivalence if and only if every $T_p(s)\to T_{p'}(s)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: these are exactly the remaining local tests, and identity on objects supplies essential surjectivity. Thus $f$ is a slice weak equivalence if and only if $Tf$ is an objectwise weak equivalence. Preservation of monomorphisms and DK cone maps in [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] then makes $T$ preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Hence $T\dashv U_S$ is Quillen; adjunction and projective fibrant lifting imply that $U_SF$ is slice-fibrant, thus a right fibration, for every objectwise Kan $F$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.4.5 dualized; Section 2.2.1, preservation part of Theorem 2.2.1.2.

proof.text: Establish the simplicial structure of the cone-defined slice model. The tensor is $X\times K\to S$ and its cotensor is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)}S$ with constant base maps. Degreewise unions show that the pushout product of two monomorphisms is a monomorphism. The final-vertex inclusion $\{n\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne], since every mapping space to $n$ in the ordered nerve is a point. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], its product with any $X$ is right anodyne, hence the section $X\cong X\times\{n\}\hookrightarrow X\times\Delta^n$ is a trivial slice cofibration by the right-anodyne clause of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. The projection $X\times\Delta^n\to X$ is therefore a weak equivalence by this weak-equivalence section and the identity composite. Slice weak equivalences are stable under every small filtered colimit: Step 2 tests them by the colimit-preserving $T$, and [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] applies objectwise, without injective transition maps. All objects are cofibrant by Step 1. Thus [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-simplicial-recognition] applies and makes this model simplicial. The fibrant objects have already been identified by the independent slice-model statement in Step 1.

All slice objects are cofibrant, and [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] identifies its fibrant objects with the right fibrations. The simplicial model axiom from Step 3, applied to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Z$ and $Y\to S$, makes $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ Kan. For a weak equivalence $f:X\to Y$ between right fibrations, the products with $\Delta^1$ are good cylinders: their endpoint pair is monomorphic, and their projection is a weak equivalence by Step 3. [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead] gives a simplicial homotopy inverse over $S$. Conversely such an inverse restricts to each strict vertex fiber; [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes each fiber map a weak homotopy equivalence. The slice node then makes $f$ a model weak equivalence. Consequently the slice node's fiberwise criterion is also exactly the equivalence criterion in $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ stated here. The simplicial model of Step 3 has every object cofibrant. Apply [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-mapping-detection] to it: its fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model], and its enriched mapping sets are exactly $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$. Thus its weak equivalences are precisely the arbitrary arrows passing all the mapping tests in the statement.

source.place: Lemmas 2.2.3.4 and 2.2.3.6; the already split Corollaries 2.2.3.12-13; simplicial model mapping test written out.

proof.text: Construct the point comparison without invoking [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], whose proof depends on the theorem being proved. Let $Q$ be the explicit pinched cosimplicial object in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] and put $V(K)=|K|_Q$. This coend preserves colimits, sends boundary inclusions to $L_nQ\hookrightarrow Q^n$, and sends $\Delta^n\to\Delta^0$ to weak equivalences because both $Q^n$ and $Q^0$ are contractible. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] in the Kan model: $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ is Quillen. The maximum-subset map of the cube lemma defines $p_K:VK\to K$. On a simplex it is a weak equivalence between contractible simplicial sets. The boundary-collapse test also makes $V$ preserve all monomorphisms. Both $V$ and the identity preserve all small colimits and monomorphisms, and $p_{\Delta^n}$ is weak for every $n$. Apply [lem-coef-sset-cellular-comparison] to the natural transformation $p:V\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$ (its first functor $V$, its second functor the identity): $p_K$ is a weak equivalence for every small $K$, including the empty set. The left derived functor of $V$ is therefore the identity on the homotopy category, so the left-derived functor is an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion], whose hypotheses are precisely this ordinary Quillen adjunction and the derived-left equivalence. For Kan $Z$, all source objects are cofibrant, so its actual counit $e_Z:V\operatorname{Sing}_QZ\to Z$ is a weak equivalence. Let $j_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Sing}_QZ$ be adjoint to $p_Z:VZ\to Z$. The triangle identity gives $e_ZVj_Z=p_Z$, so $Vj_Z$, and then $j_Z$ by the natural weak equivalences $p$, is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Propositions 2.2.2.7 and 2.2.2.9, Corollary 2.2.2.10; explicit independent point argument

proof.text:
The representable-times-$VK$ formula in [lem-coef-cone-boundary-projective-cells], followed by enriched evaluation, identifies $(U_SF)_s$ with $\operatorname{Sing}_Q(F(s))$. Step 5 supplies the natural fiberwise weak equivalence $j_{F(s)}$. Base change is strict at the level of the defining simplex families: for $u:B\to S$ a simplex over $\tau:\Delta^n\to B$ is the same transformation from the cone module for $u\tau$ to $F$, or by the universal pushout/extension property from the cone module for $\tau$ to $F\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}}$. The bijections commute with every simplex operator, enriched transformation of $F$, and iterated substitution of $u$. This gives the stated coherent base-change isomorphisms. For the constant diagram at $X$, take the map to the one-point indexing simplicial category. Composing cone arrows with this functor identifies its unstraightening over $S$ with $S\times\operatorname{Sing}_QX$: over each simplex the cone-to-point module is $Q^n$. Hence $\mathrm{id}_S\times j_X$ is the stated constant-product map. More generally this calculation with an external constant factor gives
$$U_S(F\times K)\cong U_SF\times\operatorname{Sing}_QK.$$
For an enriched transformation $F\times K\to G$, apply $U_S$ and precompose with $\mathrm{id}\times j_K$; currying gives $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(U_SF,U_SG)$. The maps $j$ respect products and identities, since they are induced by the same cosimplicial map $Q\to\Delta^\bullet$; evaluating a pair of parameters shows that composition is preserved. This is the required actual simplicial functor structure. If $F\to G$ is objectwise a weak equivalence between objectwise Kan diagrams, the fiber identifications and natural $j$ show its unstraightening is fiberwise a weak equivalence. Step 4 then makes it an equivalence of right fibrations.

Apply [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent] directly. Its $D$, projective category $\mathcal P_S$, ordered cone module $L_S$, and simplex-defined right adjoint agree with $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathsf D_S$, $T$, and $U_S$ in Steps 1-2. Its enrichment is induced by the same cosimplicial map $Q^n\to\Delta^n$ and external product construction of Step 6. Its statement therefore gives the required actual Dwyer--Kan equivalence $U_S:\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$, including weak equivalences on mapping complexes and essential surjectivity by actual simplicial homotopy equivalences over $S$. Its hypothesis is an arbitrary small simplicial base, as here. No simplex comparison, localization or descent proof is repeated in this item.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11 (printed pp. 83-85), through its existing independent DAG node.

proof.text: Derive the Quillen-equivalence criterion without a new enriched-localization input. In either simplicial model of Steps 1 and 3, product with $\Delta^1$ is a good cylinder on every cofibrant object: the simplicial model axiom makes the endpoint pair a cofibration and an endpoint inclusion trivial, so its projection is weak by two-out-of-three. [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] represents every homotopy-category map from a cofibrant object to a fibrant one by an actual map. For these good product cylinders, [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] identifies equality of represented maps exactly with simplicial homotopy. Thus the ordinary homotopy category is equivalent to $\pi_0$ of its full simplicial subcategory of bifibrant objects: full faithfulness is precisely these two cited assertions, and essential surjectivity follows by first cofibrantly and then fibrantly replacing any object, with both replacement arrows weak and the final object still cofibrant. The ordinary derived adjunction of [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] restricts on bifibrant objects to the given ordinary $U_S$, which sends projectively bifibrant diagrams to slice-bifibrant objects since all slice objects are cofibrant. Under the preceding identifications, its derived right functor is the equivalence on $\pi_0$ given by Step 7. A left adjoint of an equivalence is an equivalence (transport the adjunction by a quasi-inverse and use the ordinary Hom bijections). Hence the derived left functor is an equivalence. Apply the same counit criterion: for every fibrant $F$, $TU_SF\to F$ is weak, because $U_SF$ is cofibrant. Given $a:TX\to F$ with adjoint $b:X\to U_SF$, the adjunction equation is $a=\epsilon_F\,T(b)$. By this weak counit and two-out-of-three, $a$ is weak exactly when $T(b)$ is weak, and by the reflection test of Step 2 exactly when $b$ is weak. This proves precisely the asserted ordinary Quillen equivalence, without assuming an enriched adjunction.

source.place: Final proof of Theorem 2.2.1.2 after Proposition 2.2.3.11; Remark A.3.1.8 and the right-adjoint criterion of Proposition A.3.1.10, derived here using ordinary homotopy-category inputs.

proof.text: Reverse ordered labels. On subset-poset mapping simplices this takes a subset of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ to its reflected subset, preserves inclusion, and reverses union composition. It gives $\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$, first on simplices and then by colimits. Reversal takes a horn with missing face $i$ to the horn with missing face $n-i$, so right fibrations become left fibrations by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. It preserves monomorphisms, products and degreewise limits, and its realization is a homeomorphism by reversing barycentric coordinates; hence it preserves weak homotopy equivalences of fibers. Transport the ordinary contravariant model structure on the opposite base by this involutive equivalence. Every object remains cofibrant, and Steps 1 and 4 identify its fibrant objects and give its fiber criterion. This transported model is simplicial for the usual tensor: its weak equivalences are stable under filtered colimits by Step 3, its monomorphisms satisfy the same pushout-product calculation, and $X\times\{0\}\to X\times\Delta^n$ is trivial because reversal is the right-anodyne final-vertex product already used in Step 3. Thus [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-simplicial-recognition] applies again. Its simplicial model axiom and the good-cylinder argument of Step 4 give Kan left-fibration mapping complexes. A weak equivalence between fibrant objects has an inverse with these product-cylinder homotopies by [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead]; an inverse with such homotopies is fiberwise weak by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. The transported fiber criterion gives the converse. This proves simplicial compatibility directly with the usual tensor and mapping objects.

An $F:\mathfrak C[S]\to\mathrm{sSet}$ is a contravariant diagram on $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ using the isomorphism of Step 9. Use the ordinary cone adjunction of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] on the opposite base and the model structure of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. Compose the right adjoint $U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}$ with reversal of its output; composing its left adjoint with inverse reversal gives the ordinary adjunction asserted for $U_S^{\mathrm{cov}}$. Transport of the model structure and Step 8 make it a Quillen equivalence. On a vertex the formula is exactly $(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)_s^{\mathrm{op}}$, which represents $F(s)$ as a space, since reversal preserves the realization of a simplicial set and Step 6 gives $F(s)\to(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)_s$. Objectwise weak equivalences between Kan diagrams are preserved before reversal by Step 6, and after reversal by the fiber criterion of Step 9. The right-derived functor is therefore obtained by localizing that restriction. Apply reversal to the degreewise base-change identities in Step 6; their identity and composition equalities remain equalities. Likewise reversal of the constant-product map is $S\times X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U_S^{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathrm{const}\,X)$, with the stated fiberwise property. For size, the simplex categories, object sets, mapping sets, joins, finite products, natural-transformation equalizers and coend quotients used in the formulas are indexed by sets in $\mathcal V$ and so stay in $\mathcal V$; the collections of all such diagrams and all fibrations are placed in a larger universe. This distinction does not enlarge any constructed simplicial set.
